posts.text:
About AI and the end of the world

Lately, we’ve been hearing a lot from AI creators who are bemoaning humanity’s haste. They’ve been warning us that AI is dangerous, unpredictable, and developing too fast according to laws we don’t quite fathom. It’s time, they say, to slow down and make a pause before we feel really sorry when our intelligent brother goes berserk.

Are these fears real? Especially given that many smarty-pants like Musk and others have been saying this for a long time. The answer is simple: they’re real. By the way, I myself wrote about it in a recent article for the Expert magazine.

But… the creators of various sorts of generative AI are not being sincere. It’s not you and I or Homo sapiens as a whole that they fear for. They’re not afraid that an unhinged AI, drunk on its power, will destroy humankind. This kind of outcome is not all that likely. What’s much more realistic is a scenario where software that uses advanced AI for running a major production facility or a transport hub will cause severe damage. Such as allowing planes to collide in midair or destroying a nuclear power plant. And then there will be someone coming for the creators of generative AI – to slap them with multibillion lawsuits or simply to knock their (human) brains out.

What’s to be done then? The most obvious solution would be for countries to agree on general principles of AI regulation. That would give us all at least some chance of keeping AI development under control. But it won’t happen due to corporate greed and insatiable human passion. 

So our only hope is to throw ourselves at the mercy of the winner and count on the humanism that AI, our beloved man-made prodigy, might show us. It doesn’t have overt emotions yet, but we don’t know what this great superintelligence will be like. Let’s hope it will spare its parents…

Tokarevsky Lighthouse, Russia 🇷🇺🌊✨

Perched on the edge of the sea in Vladivostok, the Tokarevsky Lighthouse stands as one of the city’s most iconic and romantic symbols. Jutting into the waters of Amur Bay, it feels like a slender thread connecting land, sky, and the boundless ocean.

Frequently listed by travel experts and leading media as one of Russia’s most romantic spots, this lighthouse draws couples who stroll along its narrow causeway, listen to waves pounding the rocks, and witness breathtaking golden sunsets over the Sea of Japan.

Even with its popularity and steady stream of visitors, the place holds onto its magic — the wind, the salt-laced air, the cry of seabirds, and the quiet strength of the sea turn every moment here into something cinematic.

🔊 Iran para shooting team wins bronze at world championships

📌 Tehran, IRNA — Iran’s national para shooting team won a bronze medal in the mixed 50m pistol team event at the 2026 World Shooting Para Sport Championships in Changwon, South Korea, bringing the country’s medal tally to four.

Iran’s team of Nasrin Shahi, Seyyed Mohammadreza Mirshafiei and Sareh Javanmardi scored 1,596 points to finish third behind South Korea and China.
​
In the individual event, Shahi advanced to the final after finishing second in the qualifying round with 543 points. She scored 139.6 points in the final to place sixth. Mirshafiei, Javanmardi and Mostafa Khadem, who scored 530, 523, and 510 points, respectively, failed to advance to the final.
​
The Changwon championships marked the end of Iran’s campaign, with the country securing four medals: a team gold, an individual gold, an individual silver, and a team bronze.
​
Faezah Ahmadi also secured a quota place for the 2028 Paralympic Games in Los Angeles.
​
Iran competed under the name of martyr Mohammad Fattahi, with Fathollah Delfani Khan as head coach, assisted by coaches Zeinab Amini-Tabar and Zahra Ahmadi, and Dr. Nasiri as team manager.

🎙 IRGC downs advanced MQ-1 drone over Strait of Hormuz

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) has confirmed the downing of an advanced MQ-1 drone in the airspace over the Strait of Hormuz.

The IRGC announced on Monday that its Aerospace Force, operating within Iran’s integrated air defense network, has intercepted and destroyed an advanced MQ-1 drone over the Strait of Hormuz moments ago.
​
The IRGC Navy had earlier announced that it had struck and destroyed a US unmanned surface vessel at the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz.
​
The Navy added that the US “terrorist and aggressor army” had in recent days dispatched unmanned vessels to the Strait of Hormuz out of fear of approaching and confronting the Iranian forces.
